def: to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete)

occurrences.text: But as they sailed he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filled with water, and were in jeopardy.
And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,
And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
